# Skill review

This page covers the scheduler options, the spawned session's permissions, what it stages, the `/skill-review status|install|undo` procedure (including the seed check, backups, and undo), and the completion notice. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

The task-observer skill (installed separately; see its own SKILL.md) keeps an open backlog of observations about every other installed skill, meant to be reviewed on a cadence with its own `references/weekly-review.md` procedure. Once turned on, this plugin can run that procedure for you: once the backlog is due, it spawns a headless OpenCode session (`ctx.session.create` + `ctx.session.prompt`, the same v2 API the board and observer use, `lib/review.js` `run`) that loads the task-observer skill and works through a bounded slice of the oldest open observations, then tracks that session through to completion.

## Scheduler options

`REVIEW_DEFAULTS` (`lib/review.js`):

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "cadenceDays": 7,
  "sliceSize": 10,
  "cooldownHours": 24,
  "timeoutMinutes": 90,
  "startupDelaySeconds": 120,
  "pollMinutes": 15,
  "model": null,
  "agent": null,
  "externalDirectories": []
}
```

`review.enabled` is `false` by default; unlike the maintenance sweep, which writes automatically by default, a scheduled review spawns a real headless session that works for a while, so this one stays opt-in. `/skill-review` triggers one run on demand (ignoring the cadence and cooldown, but not a review already in progress), independent of `review.enabled`.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cadenceDays` | Minimum days since the last review before another one is due. |
| `sliceSize` | How many of the oldest open observations (by id, plus anything that restates one of them) one review run is scoped to. |
| `cooldownHours` | Minimum time between attempts, independent of the cadence (covers a run that was skipped or failed quickly). |
| `timeoutMinutes` | How long a lock (and the spawned session itself) is allowed to run before it is considered stale, replaceable by the next attempt, and interrupted. |
| `startupDelaySeconds` | How long after plugin setup the first scheduled check runs. |
| `pollMinutes` | How often the scheduled check re-runs after that first one. |
| `model` | `"provider/model"` for the spawned session. Unset uses the host's default model. |
| `agent` | Agent name for the spawned session. Unset uses the host's default agent. |
| `externalDirectories` | Extra absolute paths (or ones starting with `~/`) the spawned session may read from outside the task-observer workspace, beyond `~/.config/opencode` and `~/.cache/opencode/npm` (always allowed, so the session can load skills and plugin code). |

The lock (`review-lock.json`) and the append-only attempt log (`review-runs.log`) both live under `<task-observer root>/skill-observations/.mighty-instincts/`, next to (never inside) the skill's own `skill-observations/` state, since several OpenCode instances on the same machine can share that workspace: the lock is created with an exclusive write (`lib/review.js` `createLockFile`), so whichever instance wins the race blocks every other one until it finishes or its `timeoutMinutes` elapses.

## Permissions of the spawned session

Last-match-wins, OpenCode 2's own resolution order (`lib/review.js` `buildReviewPermissions`):

- Editing is denied everywhere except inside the task-observer workspace (`root`).
- Reading outside the workspace is denied everywhere except `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.cache/opencode/npm`, and anything listed in `review.externalDirectories`.
- Shell is allowed outright, since the review procedure runs bash snippets and a headless session has nobody to answer an "ask" permission prompt.

The edit deny and the prompt's own instructions are what actually keep the review inside the workspace; shell can still write elsewhere through means an edit permission does not cover.

## What it stages

The session is instructed (`lib/review.js` `buildReviewPrompt`) to:

- Load the task-observer skill, then its `references/weekly-review.md`, in scheduled autonomous mode.
- Scope the run to the `sliceSize` oldest open observations by id, plus any open observation that restates one of them.
- Stage every skill change as a copy under `<root>/skill-updates/<date>/`, and record it in `<root>/skill-updates/PENDING.md`.
- Never edit an installed skill file, an AGENTS.md, or anything outside the workspace (enforced by the permission deny above too).
- Set each reviewed observation's status (`actioned`, `declined`, `parked`, or `superseded`) with `resolved:`/`resolution:`; anything needing the owner's decision stays open, listed under "Skipped (needs manual review)".
- Finish by writing today's date to `last-review-date.txt` and the review summary to `skill-observations/review-reports/<date>.md`.

## `/skill-review status|install|undo`

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/skill-review` | Run the backlog review now in a headless session, ignoring the cadence and cooldown (but not a review already in progress) (`lib/commands-maintain.js` `buildSkillReviewCommand`). |
| `/skill-review status` | Report the open count, staged count, last review date, whether a run is due, and any in-flight session id (`lib/commands-maintain.js` `formatReviewStatus`). |
| `/skill-review install [n\|all]` | With no argument, list staged updates. `install <n>` or `install all` installs them (see "Install procedure" below). |
| `/skill-review undo` | Reverts the most recently installed update, unconditionally overwriting any hand edit made to the live file since. |

### Install procedure, including the seed check

For each staged skill copy (`<root>/skill-updates/<entry.id>/<skill>/SKILL.md`), `planInstall` (`lib/review-install.js`) checks whether the live skill file still matches a "seed" snapshot: a `<skill>.pre-*` sibling directory, or the specific one an "Install" clause in the batch's own README/PENDING.md names. That seed is staged by the task-observer skill's own weekly-review procedure as its diff baseline when it drafts an update, not by this plugin: `collectSeedCandidates` only ever reads whichever seed the procedure already left behind. If the live file's content equals a seed snapshot exactly, the install proceeds; if it does not (someone edited the live file by hand since staging), the install is refused for that skill, with a `+N/-N` line-diff summary against the seed. When no seed snapshot can be found at all (the procedure never staged one for this skill, or it has since been removed), the install is refused with "no seed snapshot found for this skill" instead.

"Live" here means `~/.config/opencode/skills`, resolved through its own realpath first (`resolveLiveSkillsDir`): a symlinked or dotfiles-managed `~/.config/opencode` is checked through to the real directory it points at, falling back to the unresolved path if that lookup itself fails.

An entry installs atomically or not at all: if any staged skill in it fails the seed check, the whole entry is refused, nothing is written (`lib/review-install.js`).

### Backups and undo

Installing backs up the live file's current content to `<root>/skill-updates/backups/<backupDirName>/<skill>/SKILL.md` before writing the staged copy over it, then records the operation (including that backup directory name) in `<root>/skill-updates/backups/.install-log.json` (`lib/review-install.js` `applyInstall`). `/skill-review undo` pops the most recent entry from that log and restores every one of its skills from its own backup directory, then marks the entry `[undone <date> by mighty-instincts]` in PENDING.md so it is staged again (`lib/review-install.js` `undoLast`). A second `undo` reaches back to whichever operation is now last, so two installs of the same skill chain back correctly.

Each install or undo also appends an annotation to the entry's own PENDING.md heading (`[installed <date> by mighty-instincts]` or `[undone <date> by mighty-instincts]`), which always wins over the file's own free-text status phrase when deciding whether an entry is still "staged" (`lib/review-install.js` `parsePending`/`isStagedHeading`).

## Completion notice

A *scheduled* review (nobody gave `run()` a sessionID to reply to) posts a completion notice once the session finishes, to the newest top-level session the host currently lists, excluding the review session itself (`lib/review.js` `postCompletionNotice`, `lib/review.js` `newestTopLevelSessionID`): "Skill review finished: `<N>` staged update(s) await /skill-review install". This needs `ctx.session.list`: when the host has no such method, the call fails, or the list has no eligible session once the review session itself is excluded, the notice is only logged (`console.warn`), never posted anywhere. `ctx.session.list` is not scoped to one project, so the session it notifies can belong to a different project than the one the review ran against. A manual `/skill-review` already told the person who typed it that the session started; its own completion is theirs to check with `/skill-review status`. A forced run refuses outright when there is nothing open to review, regardless of `force` (`lib/review.js`).

# Continuous Learning v2.1 - Instinct
-Based Architecture

An advanced learning system that turns your Claude Code sessions into reusable knowledge through atomic "instincts" - small learned behaviors with confidence scoring.

**v2.1** adds **project-scoped instincts** — React patterns stay in your React project, Python conventions stay in your Python project, and universal patterns (like "always validate input") are shared globally.

## When to Activate

- Setting up automatic learning from Claude Code sessions
- Configuring instinct-based behavior extraction via hooks
- Tuning confidence thresholds for learned behaviors
- Reviewing, exporting, or importing instinct libraries
- Evolving instincts into full skills, commands, or agents
- Managing project-scoped vs global instincts
- Promoting instincts from project to global scope

## What's New in v2.1

| Feature | v2.0 | v2.1 |
|---------|------|------|
| Storage | Global (`~/.claude/homunculus/`) | Project-scoped (`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/projects/<hash>/`) |
| Scope | All instincts apply everywhere | Project-scoped + global |
| Detection | None | git remote URL / repo path |
| Promotion | N/A | Project → global when seen in 2+ projects |
| Commands | 4 (status/evolve/export/import) | 6 (+promote/projects) |
| Cross-project | Contamination risk | Isolated by default |

## What's New in v2 (vs v1)

| Feature | v1 | v2 |
|---------|----|----|
| Observation | Stop hook (session end) | PreToolUse/PostToolUse (100% reliable) |
| Analysis | Main context | Background agent (Haiku) |
| Granularity | Full skills | Atomic "instincts" |
| Confidence | None | 0.3-0.9 weighted |
| Evolution | Direct to skill | Instincts -> cluster -> skill/command/agent |
| Sharing | None | Export/import instincts |

## The Instinct Model

An instinct is a small learned behavior:

```yaml
---
id: prefer-functional-style
trigger: "when writing new functions"
confidence: 0.7
domain: "code-style"
source: "session-observation"
scope: project
project_id: "a1b2c3d4e5f6"
project_name: "my-react-app"
---

# Prefer Functional Style

## Action
Use functional patterns over classes when appropriate.

## Evidence
- Observed 5 instances of functional pattern preference
- User corrected class-based approach to functional on 2025-01-15
```

**Properties:**
- **Atomic** -- one trigger, one action
- **Confidence-weighted** -- 0.3 = tentative, 0.9 = near certain
- **Domain-tagged** -- code-style, testing, git, debugging, workflow, etc.
- **Evidence-backed** -- tracks what observations created it
- **Scope-aware** -- `project` (default) or `global`

## How It Works

```
Session Activity (in a git repo)
      |
      | Hooks capture prompts + tool use (100% reliable)
      | + detect project context (git remote / repo path)
      v
+---------------------------------------------+
|  projects/<project-hash>/observations.jsonl  |
|   (prompts, tool calls, outcomes, project)   |
+---------------------------------------------+
      |
      | Observer agent reads (background, Haiku)
      v
+---------------------------------------------+
|          PATTERN DETECTION                   |
|   * User corrections -> instinct             |
|   * Error resolutions -> instinct            |
|   * Repeated workflows -> instinct           |
|   * Scope decision: project or global?       |
+---------------------------------------------+
      |
      | Creates/updates
      v
+---------------------------------------------+
|  projects/<project-hash>/instincts/personal/ |
|   * prefer-functional.yaml (0.7) [project]   |
|   * use-react-hooks.yaml (0.9) [project]     |
+---------------------------------------------+
|  instincts/personal/  (GLOBAL)               |
|   * always-validate-input.yaml (0.85) [global]|
|   * grep-before-edit.yaml (0.6) [global]     |
+---------------------------------------------+
      |
      | /evolve clusters + /promote
      v
+---------------------------------------------+
|  projects/<hash>/evolved/ (project-scoped)   |
|  evolved/ (global)                           |
|   * commands/new-feature.md                  |
|   * skills/testing-workflow.md               |
|   * agents/refactor-specialist.md            |
+---------------------------------------------+
```

## Project Detection

The system automatically detects your current project:

1. **`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` env var** (highest priority) -- honored as an explicit override even when the directory is not a git repo (hashed by its absolute path)
2. **`git remote get-url origin`** -- hashed to create a portable project ID (same repo on different machines gets the same ID)
3. **`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`** -- fallback using repo path (machine-specific)
4. **Global fallback** -- if no project is detected, instincts go to global scope

Each project gets a 12-character hash ID (e.g., `a1b2c3d4e5f6`). A registry file at `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/projects.json` maps IDs to human-readable names.

### Data Directory

Continuous-learning-v2 stores observer data outside `~/.claude` so Claude Code's sensitive-path guard does not block background instinct writes:

1. `CLV2_HOMUNCULUS_DIR` when set to an absolute path
2. `$XDG_DATA_HOME/ecc-homunculus`
3. `$HOME/.local/share/ecc-homunculus`

Existing users with data at `~/.claude/homunculus` can migrate once:

```bash
bash skills/continuous-learning-v2/scripts/migrate-homunculus.sh
```

## Quick Start

### 1. Enable Observation Hooks

**If installed as a plugin** (recommended):

No extra `settings.json` hook block is required. Claude Code v2.1+ auto-loads the plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, and `observe.sh` is already registered there.

If you previously copied `observe.sh` into `~/.claude/settings.json`, remove that duplicate `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` block. Duplicating the plugin hook causes double execution and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolution errors because that variable is only available inside plugin-managed `hooks/hooks.json` entries.

**If installed manually** to `~/.claude/skills`, add this to your `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "*",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "~/.claude/skills/continuous-learning-v2/hooks/observe.sh"
      }]
    }],
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "*",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "~/.claude/skills/continuous-learning-v2/hooks/observe.sh"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### 2. Initialize Directory Structure

The system creates directories automatically on first use, but you can also create them manually:

```bash
# Global directories
mkdir -p "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus"/{instincts/{personal,inherited},evolved/{agents,skills,commands},projects}

# Project directories are auto-created when the hook first runs in a git repo
```

### 3. Use the Instinct Commands

```bash
/instinct-status     # Show learned instincts (project + global)
/evolve              # Cluster related instincts into skills/commands
/instinct-export     # Export instincts to file
/instinct-import     # Import instincts from others
/promote             # Promote project instincts to global scope
/projects            # List all known projects and their instinct counts
```

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/instinct-status` | Show all instincts (project-scoped + global) with confidence |
| `/evolve` | Cluster related instincts into skills/commands, suggest promotions |
| `/instinct-export` | Export instincts (filterable by scope/domain) |
| `/instinct-import <file>` | Import instincts with scope control |
| `/promote [id]` | Promote project instincts to global scope |
| `/projects` | List all known projects and their instinct counts |

## Configuration

Edit `config.json` to control the background observer:

```json
{
  "version": "2.1",
  "observer": {
    "enabled": false,
    "run_interval_minutes": 5,
    "min_observations_to_analyze": 20
  }
}
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `observer.enabled` | `false` | Enable the background observer agent |
| `observer.run_interval_minutes` | `5` | How often the observer analyzes observations |
| `observer.min_observations_to_analyze` | `20` | Minimum observations before analysis runs |

Other behavior (observation capture, instinct thresholds, project scoping, promotion criteria) is configured via code defaults in `instinct-cli.py` and `observe.sh`.

### Observer platform support

The background observer requires WSL2, Linux, or macOS. On native Windows
(Git Bash / MSYS2) it starts and reports success, but the process is killed
when the spawning hook exits and its Job Object closes, so no analysis ever
runs — setting `observer.enabled: true` there is effectively a no-op
(see issue #2489).

`observe.sh` detects this on the following hook invocation and writes an
explanatory warning to `observer-start.log` once the observer has failed to
survive several times in a row.

| Env var | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `ECC_OBSERVER_NOSURVIVE_WARN_AFTER` | `3` | Consecutive non-survivals before the warning is logged |

## File Structure

```
${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/
+-- identity.json           # Your profile, technical level
+-- projects.json           # Registry: project hash -> name/path/remote
+-- observations.jsonl      # Global observations (fallback)
+-- instincts/
|   +-- personal/           # Global auto-learned instincts
|   +-- inherited/          # Global imported instincts
+-- evolved/
|   +-- agents/             # Global generated agents
|   +-- skills/             # Global generated skills
|   +-- commands/           # Global generated commands
+-- projects/
    +-- a1b2c3d4e5f6/       # Project hash (from git remote URL)
    |   +-- project.json    # Per-project metadata mirror (id/name/root/remote)
    |   +-- observations.jsonl
    |   +-- observations.archive/
    |   +-- instincts/
    |   |   +-- personal/   # Project-specific auto-learned
    |   |   +-- inherited/  # Project-specific imported
    |   +-- evolved/
    |       +-- skills/
    |       +-- commands/
    |       +-- agents/
    +-- f6e5d4c3b2a1/       # Another project
        +-- ...
```

## Scope Decision Guide

| Pattern Type | Scope | Examples |
|-------------|-------|---------|
| Language/framework conventions | **project** | "Use React hooks", "Follow Django REST patterns" |
| File structure preferences | **project** | "Tests in `__tests__`/", "Components in src/components/" |
| Code style | **project** | "Use functional style", "Prefer dataclasses" |
| Error handling strategies | **project** | "Use Result type for errors" |
| Security practices | **global** | "Validate user input", "Sanitize SQL" |
| General best practices | **global** | "Write tests first", "Always handle errors" |
| Tool workflow preferences | **global** | "Grep before Edit", "Read before Write" |
| Git practices | **global** | "Conventional commits", "Small focused commits" |

## Instinct Promotion (Project -> Global)

When the same instinct appears in multiple projects with high confidence, it's a candidate for promotion to global scope.

**Auto-promotion criteria:**
- Same instinct ID in 2+ projects
- Average confidence >= 0.8

**How to promote:**

```bash
# Promote a specific instinct
python3 instinct-cli.py promote prefer-explicit-errors

# Auto-promote all qualifying instincts
python3 instinct-cli.py promote

# Preview without changes
python3 instinct-cli.py promote --dry-run
```

The `/evolve` command also suggests promotion candidates.

## Confidence Scoring

Confidence evolves over time:

| Score | Meaning | Behavior |
|-------|---------|----------|
| 0.3 | Tentative | Suggested but not enforced |
| 0.5 | Moderate | Applied when relevant |
| 0.7 | Strong | Auto-approved for application |
| 0.9 | Near-certain | Core behavior |

**Confidence increases** when:
- Pattern is repeatedly observed
- User doesn't correct the suggested behavior
- Similar instincts from other sources agree

**Confidence decreases** when:
- User explicitly corrects the behavior
- Pattern isn't observed for extended periods
- Contradicting evidence appears

## Why Hooks vs Skills for Observation?

> "v1 relied on skills to observe. Skills are probabilistic -- they fire ~50-80% of the time based on Claude's judgment."

Hooks fire **100% of the time**, deterministically. This means:
- Every tool call is observed
- No patterns are missed
- Learning is comprehensive

## Backward Compatibility

v2.1 is fully compatible with v2.0 and v1:
- Existing global instincts can be migrated from `~/.claude/homunculus/instincts/` with `scripts/migrate-homunculus.sh`
- Existing `~/.claude/skills/learned/` skills from v1 still work
- Stop hook still runs (but now also feeds into v2)
- Gradual migration: run both in parallel

## Privacy

- Observations stay **local** on your machine
- Project-scoped instincts are isolated per project
- Only **instincts** (patterns) can be exported — not raw observations
- No actual code or conversation content is shared
- You control what gets exported and promoted

# mighty-instincts

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) V2 plugin that observes session activity (tool calls and prompts) into a per-project log, distils it into small learned "instincts," and exposes [ECC](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC)'s instinct CLI as slash commands.

On by default: the maintenance sweep (`promote`, `prune`, `decay`, `dedupe`, `evolve`, `repair`, `cleanupProjects`, all `true` in `MAINTENANCE_DEFAULTS`) keeps instinct files tidy with no input from you, and prompt injection (`inject.enabled: true`) adds a small `<instincts>` block to every outgoing model request, built fresh from whatever instinct files already exist, at no cost in model calls. Off by default: the observer itself (`observer.enabled: false`, the one background step that actually calls a model and writes new instincts) and the scheduled skill-review backlog check (`review.enabled: false`; `/skill-review` still runs one on demand regardless). Nothing the `evolve` step proposes ever becomes a real skill, command, agent, or AGENTS.md rule by itself either (`prune.auto: false` too): it only ever *proposes* a candidate, and installing, rejecting, or archiving one is always a command you type.

## Install

> `opencode-instincts` was this package's previous name. If your `opencode.json` still references it, replace it with `mighty-instincts`.

Add the plugin to your `opencode.json`, project-local or global at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["mighty-instincts"]
}
```

To set options, use the object form instead of the bare string:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "mighty-instincts", "options": { "observer": { "enabled": true, "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" } } }
  ]
}
```

Restart OpenCode. Requires Python 3 on `PATH` (the plugin runs ECC's vendored `instinct-cli.py` as a subprocess; nothing else is installed). When Python cannot be found or the project cannot otherwise be resolved, this plugin logs a warning and falls back to the shared global instinct bucket instead of failing; the board's Health block also flags it ("python not found: habits are saved to the shared global bucket; set the python option"). On the OpenCode 2 TUI the sidebar board (`mighty-instincts/tui`) loads alongside the server plugin automatically; no extra configuration is needed.

A typo or a wrong-typed option is always reported, not silently dropped: `validateOptions` warns about each unknown key (with a spelling suggestion for a likely typo) or wrongly-typed known key, both to the console and to the board's Health block.

## Options

All options are optional; this is `mergeOptions({})` from `lib/plugin.js`, the real computed defaults (same tree as `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, also exported):

```json
{
  "disabled": false,
  "python": "python3",
  "observePrompts": true,
  "ignoreTools": ["todowrite", "todoread", "question", "instincts"],
  "ignoreAgents": [],
  "observer": { "enabled": false, "runIntervalMinutes": 15, "minObservations": 40, "maxAnalysisLines": 300, "maxAnalysisBytes": 32768, "notify": true },
  "inject": { "enabled": true, "max": 5, "minConfidence": 0.8, "exclude": [] },
  "board": { "enabled": true, "sections": { "instincts": true, "observations": true, "evals": true }, "refreshSeconds": 30, "observationsRoot": null, "evalRoots": null, "compact": false },
  "maintenance": { "intervalHours": 24, "dryRun": false, "promote": true, "prune": true, "decay": true, "dedupe": true, "evolve": true, "repair": true, "cleanupProjects": true },
  "review": { "enabled": false, "cadenceDays": 7, "sliceSize": 10, "cooldownHours": 24, "timeoutMinutes": 90, "startupDelaySeconds": 120, "pollMinutes": 15, "model": null, "agent": null, "externalDirectories": [] },
  "evolve": { "targets": { "skill": null, "command": null, "agent": null, "rule": null } },
  "prune": { "unusedDays": 30, "auto": false }
}
```

Two keys are omitted above because JSON cannot carry `undefined`: `dataDir` (default unset) and `observer.model` (default unset; required before the observer actually runs).

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `disabled` | Skip registering everything (hooks, commands, tool, board, maintenance). |
| `dataDir` | Absolute path for ECC's data directory instead of the default; relative values are ignored with a warning. |
| `python` | Python interpreter to run `instinct-cli.py` with. |
| `observePrompts` | Record user prompt text (scrubbed, clipped) as `user_prompt` observations. |
| `ignoreTools` / `ignoreAgents` | Tool names / agent names to never observe. |
| `observer.*` | Background distillation run: model requirement, backoff, zero-write damper, notify rule. See [docs/observer.md](docs/observer.md). |
| `inject.*` | Prompt injection: block size, confidence floor, exclude list. See [docs/instinct.md](docs/instinct.md). |
| `maintenance.*` | The always-on sweep's own steps and their on/off switches, plus `dryRun` and `intervalHours`. See [docs/maintenance.md](docs/maintenance.md). |
| `review.*` | Scheduled task-observer backlog review. See [docs/skill-review.md](docs/skill-review.md). |
| `evolve.targets.*` | Overrides for where `/evolve ... install` writes a candidate (skill/command/agent directory, or the rule file in place of AGENTS.md). See [docs/evolve.md](docs/evolve.md). |
| `prune.unusedDays` / `.auto` | How long an installed, unused candidate is flagged before (opt-in) auto-archiving. See [docs/evolve.md](docs/evolve.md). |
| `board.*` | Sidebar panel and `/board` on/off, which sections show, refresh cadence, and the task-observer/skill-eval search roots. See [docs/board.md](docs/board.md). |

The default `ignoreTools` list keeps the plugin from observing its own tool and the host's own todo/question tools; `ignoreAgents` is empty by default, so every agent (including subagents) is observed unless you add one.

To turn the observer and the scheduled skill review on together:

```json
{
  "observer": { "enabled": true, "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" },
  "review": { "enabled": true, "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" }
}
```

Set `"maintenance": { "dryRun": true }` to see exactly what the next sweep would do without changing anything: every line it would otherwise log is prefixed `would` instead, with nothing written, moved, or deleted. `/maintain --dry-run` gets the same preview on demand.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/board` | Show the instinct board summary as plain text. See [docs/board.md](docs/board.md). |
| `/evolve [...]` | Dashboard, detail, install, reject, archive, 'now', 'clusters', and 'purge' (move the drafts it does not list aside) for evolve candidates (run with no arguments for the grammar's own dashboard). See [docs/evolve.md](docs/evolve.md). |
| `/instinct [...]` | ECC instinct status, per-habit feedback (keep/wrong/mute/unmute), the observer's on/off switch, doctor, and why (what got injected). Run with no arguments, or 'help', for the full verb list. See [docs/instinct.md](docs/instinct.md). |
| `/maintain [...]` | Run the maintenance sweep now (promote/prune/decay/evolve/repair/cleanup); `--dry-run` previews every step; `prune [--dry-run]` runs only the pending-instinct prune. See [docs/maintenance.md](docs/maintenance.md). |
| `/promote [--yes]` | Preview (default) or run (`--yes`) promoting project-scoped instincts that qualify to global scope. See [docs/maintenance.md](docs/maintenance.md). |
| `/skill-review [...]` | Run the task-observer backlog review now (headless session); `status`, `install [n\|all]`, and `undo` manage staged skill updates. See [docs/skill-review.md](docs/skill-review.md). |

Eleven hyphenated commands remain registered for one release as deprecated aliases that forward their old argv shape into the grammar above, each prefixing its reply with a deprecation notice: `/evolve-list`, `/evolve-show`, `/evolve-install`, `/evolve-reject`, and `/evolve-archive` forward into `/evolve`; `/instinct-status`, `/instinct-import`, `/instinct-export`, and `/instinct-projects` forward into `/instinct`; `/instinct-observe` forwards into `/instinct observe`; `/instinct-prune` forwards into `/maintain prune`.

The plugin also registers a model-callable `instincts` tool, a read-only subset of the CLI the agent can call mid-turn: status, projects, export, evolve preview, promote (dry-run only), and prune (dry-run only); it never writes, imports, deletes, or passes `--force`. Its status answer opens with the version the session runs (`plugin: mighty-instincts@<version>`, the form `opencode.json` pins, so a stale session shows against the pin).

On the OpenCode 2 TUI, typing `/evolve` with no arguments is meant to open a pick-a-candidate / pick-an-action / confirm dialog instead of the text dashboard, so a human never has to type an id or a number by hand; typed arguments (`/evolve 2 install`) still go straight to the server command unchanged. Whether the TUI layer or the server command wins the shared `/evolve` name could not be confirmed without a live host; if the host routes the name to the server command instead, the text dashboard appears. See [docs/evolve.md](docs/evolve.md).

Every command above posts its reply back into the session as a synthetic message with `resume: true`, so it surfaces immediately instead of waiting for the next turn; none of them start a model turn. The background observer's own notify message (after an unprompted run nobody is necessarily watching for) keeps `resume: false` instead.

## The board

On the OpenCode 2 TUI, a small, collapsible sidebar panel summarises three sources in plain language: Learned habits (this plugin's own instincts and observer status), Skill notes (the task-observer skill's open backlog), and Skill test (skill-creator's latest benchmark result), plus a Health block whenever something needs attention. ```

`/board`'s own chat reply says the same facts in prose instead:


## Privacy

- Observations contain scrubbed tool inputs/outputs and prompt text (the same credential-redaction pattern ECC's shell hook uses), clipped to a few thousand characters each.
- Everything stays on disk under the data directory (see [docs/data-layout.md](docs/data-layout.md)). This plugin talks to a model in two places: the one `generate.text` call per observer run (on whichever model `observer.model` names), and the headless session `/skill-review` spawns (on `review.model`, or the host's own default model when that is unset). Prompt injection and the maintenance loop never call a model.
- Only instincts (small learned patterns), never raw observations, can be exported with `/instinct export`.
- The board state file contains only counts, dates, and short status strings (no observation or finding text).
- `/instinct mute`/`wrong`/`observer on|off` are the only settings persisted outside `opencode.json`, in a small per-project `.settings.json` next to the observation log (see [docs/data-layout.md](docs/data-layout.md)); nothing in it is sent anywhere either.

## Development

- `npm test` runs the smoke suite (`smoke-test.mjs`) under both `node` and `bun`, exercising the library modules directly against real temp data directories, with no plugin host involved.
- `npm run check` (`scripts/check.sh`) is the one gate `.githooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/release.sh`, and CI all run through, in order: `syntax` (`node --check` on every tracked `.js`/`.mjs` file), `smoke` (the same two-runtime suite `npm test` runs), `dashes` (no em dash or en dash in tracked source, docs, or config files, proven against its own self-test fixture first), and `skeleton` (diffs the release/check/hook scripts against the sibling plugin repo that shares this exact skeleton, skipped with a notice when that sibling cannot be found).
- `npm run hooks` installs the fast pre-commit hook (`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`), which runs only the `syntax` and `dashes` stages against the staged blobs, so a partially staged file is judged on what is actually about to be committed.
- `scripts/sync-skeleton.sh --check`/`--apply` keeps that shared skeleton in sync with the sibling repo (resolved from `--sibling`, then `$MIGHTY_SIBLING_DIR`, then a `mighty-*` directory next to this repo or under `~/dev`); `--apply` copies this repo's own skeleton files onto the sibling with the package name swapped, and never commits anything itself.
- `scripts/release.sh <version>` gates a release on, in order: the current branch being `main` with `HEAD` matching `origin/main` after a fetch, a clean tree apart from `package.json`, `scripts/check.sh` passing in full, then `npm version`, commit, tag, push, and polling both the pushed commit's CI run and npm's published version before reporting success.

# Board

This page covers the sidebar board panel and the `/board` chat summary: every row, glyph, hint, and the Health block. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

## What writes it, and how often

The server half (`lib/board.js`) computes a per-project `board-state.json` on plugin setup, after every observer run, and on a timer (`board.refreshSeconds`, default 30 seconds). The TUI sidebar panel polls that same file every 1 second; `/board` reads it fresh on request. Both the sidebar panel (`sidebar.js`) and `/board` (`lib/commands.js`'s `buildBoardCommand`, `lib/board-format.js`) render from the exact same block model (`lib/board-text.js`), so the two never disagree about what a given state means. They just say it differently: the sidebar is a dot-aligned 36-column panel, `/board` is a short, explanatory chat paragraph per block.

## Glyphs

Every block has a status circle (`lib/board-text.js` `GLYPH_CHAR`):

| Glyph | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `\u25cf` solid (active colour) | Active and healthy. |
| `\u25cf` solid (attention colour) | Needs attention. |
| `\u25cb` hollow | Stale: no data yet, or too old to trust. |

The legend row at the bottom of an expanded panel (`lib/board-text.js` `LEGEND`) spells all three out.

## The sidebar layout

Fully expanded, the panel reads like this (`lib/board.js` builds the facts, `lib/board-text.js` builds the rows, `sidebar.js` lays them out as boxes):

```
▾ Mighty Instincts v0.11.2
  ▾ Learned habits               ● 16
      habits in prompts               6
      used today / this week      2 / 9
      ready to share globally         4
        /promote
      next learning run            in 3m
      1 shell-safety-habits [rule], 3 habits: /evolve 1
      installed from habits            1 (0 unused): /evolve
  ▾ Skill notes                  ● 398
      open                           398
      added this week                158
      last reviewed                 never
  ▾ Skill test (pr)               ○ 2d
      new                           100%
      old                           100%
      verdict                   saturated
  ▾ Health                        ● 1
      observer enabled with no model: set observer.model
```

The panel header and every block title are clickable, collapsing the whole panel or just that block down to one line; the header also shows the installed version (`lib/pkg.js`'s `PKG_VERSION`). A Health row only ever appears when `collectHealth` actually found something to flag (`lib/board-text.js` `buildHealthBlock`); a project with nothing misconfigured never shows that block at all.

## Rows, by block

### Learned habits (`lib/board-text.js` `buildInstinctsBlock`)

| Row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| headline count | Every instinct this project can see: project + inherited + global (`lib/board.js`). |
| **habits in prompts** | A live eligibility count for injection right now: confidence `>= inject.minConfidence`, not excluded, not pending (`lib/board.js`, reusing `lib/inject.js`'s own `selectForInjection`). Not a per-day tally; it can rise or fall between refreshes as instincts are learned, decayed, or promoted. |
| **used today / this week** | How many times an included or still-pending instinct's trigger actually matched something typed today, and the same total summed over the last 7 days (`lib/activity.js`'s `firedToday`/`firedThisWeek`). |
| **ready to share globally** | The real cross-project `promoteStep` dry-run count (`lib/board.js` `countPromoteReady`/`countPromoteReadyCached`), not a confidence-only guess: nonzero here is exactly how many instincts `/promote` would copy right now. Shows a `/promote` hint when nonzero (`lib/board-text.js`). |
| **next learning run** | One of several states, see "Next learning run" below (`lib/board-text.js`). |
| numbered candidate rows | Up to 3 of the still-`proposed` evolve candidates (`PROPOSED_ROWS_SHOWN`, `lib/board-text.js`), each `<n> <id> [<kind>], <count> habits: /evolve <n>`; `<n>` is a valid `/evolve <n>` pick right away. |
| **installed from habits** | How many candidates are installed as a real skill, command, agent, or AGENTS.md rule, with how many of those have had zero uses in `prune.unusedDays` days (default 30) in parentheses (`lib/board-text.js`). |
| **awaiting first use** | Instincts the observer was not confident enough about to call "learned" yet (the 50% rule; see [observer.md](observer.md)); they graduate once used once (`lib/board-text.js`). |
| **kept tidy** | What the maintenance loop did in the last 7 days: `promoted`, `archived`, `merged`, `pruned`, `candidates`, `repaired`, `cleaned`, whichever are nonzero (`lib/board-text.js` `formatKeptTidy`). |
| top-habits rows | The top 5 instincts this project trusts most, by confidence, `<pct>% <id>` (`TOP_HABITS_SHOWN`, `lib/board-text.js`). |

#### Next learning run

Reads one of (`lib/board-text.js`):

- `ready`, once both the interval and the observation-count gates have cleared.
- `in <duration>`, while only the interval is still outstanding.
- `after N more events (M so far)`, once the interval has elapsed but not enough new activity has accumulated yet.
- `learning off: /instinct observer on (needs observer.model)`, while `observer.enabled` is `false`.
- `learning paused: set observer.model`, once a run has discovered the model option is unset.
- `last learning run failed (N), retry <relative>`, after a consecutive `generate.text` failure.

The paused/failed hints can appear alongside any of the first three, since the backoff clock can clear before a scheduled run next succeeds. See [observer.md](observer.md) for the full gate.

### Skill notes (`lib/board-text.js` `buildObservationsBlock`)

The task-observer skill's own open backlog (read-only; this plugin never writes into that skill's workspace, `lib/board-observations.js`):

| Row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **open** | Observations with `status: open` (or no status line at all). |
| **added this week** | Opened in the last 7 days. |
| **last reviewed** | When the backlog was last reviewed by a human, or `never`. |
| **staged skill updates** (hint, only when nonzero) | Drafted skill updates sitting in `skill-updates/PENDING.md`, waiting for a human to run `/skill-review install` (`lib/board-text.js`). A nonzero count also flips this block's glyph to attention. |

The glyph reads attention when `open > 100` and the last review is never or more than 7 days old (`lib/board-observations.js` `WARNING_OPEN_THRESHOLD`/`WARNING_REVIEW_DAYS`), or when anything is staged.

### Skill test (`lib/board-text.js` `buildEvalsBlock`)

The newest skill-creator benchmark found under the configured eval roots (see [data-layout.md](data-layout.md) for the search order). Named `Skill test (<skill>)` once a benchmark exists; `Skill test` with headline `none` otherwise.

| Row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **with skill** / **without**, or **new** / **old** | The two pass rates compared: skill included vs. removed, or (skill-creator's `old_skill` naming) the edited skill vs. its own previous version. |
| **verdict** | `saturated` (both runs already at or above 99.5%, `EVAL_SATURATED_THRESHOLD`, so the evals cannot separate them at all), `no change` (a difference under 5 points, `EVAL_NO_DIFFERENCE_THRESHOLD`, but not at the ceiling), `improved` (5+ points higher; the only verdict with an active glyph, and only while the benchmark is still fresh), or `worse` (5+ points lower). |

A benchmark older than 7 days (`EVAL_STALE_MS`) reads stale regardless of verdict.

### Health (`lib/health.js` `collectHealth`)

Shown only when there is something to flag:

| Check | Message |
| --- | --- |
| python not found | "python not found: habits are saved to the shared global bucket; set the python option" |
| data dir not writable | "data dir not writable: `<path>`" |
| `board.observationsRoot` configured but missing | "observationsRoot configured but missing: `<path>`" (only once the user has pointed it somewhere; the unconfigured default never existing yet is not flagged) |
| observer enabled with no model | "observer enabled with no model: set observer.model" |
| no eval found under any configured root | "eval roots missing: no skill-creator benchmark found under `<roots>`" (informational, not urgent) |
| an option validation warning | Whatever `lib/plugin.js`'s `validateOptions` found (an unknown key, or a value of the wrong type) |

# Data layout

This page lists every file this plugin writes, with its path. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

Everything lands in ECC's existing on-disk layout so `instinct-cli.py` (and anything else that reads it) sees the same data; the only additions are the bookkeeping files marked below. Project identity (`<project-hash>`) is resolved by calling ECC's own `detect_project()` in `vendor/ecc/instinct-cli.py` (`lib/project.js`), so this plugin and the CLI agree unless resolution fails, in which case a warning is logged and the shared `global` bucket is used (`lib/project.js` `globalFallback`).

The root directory below is the `dataDir` option when set (an absolute path), else `$XDG_DATA_HOME/ecc-homunculus`, else `~/.local/share/ecc-homunculus` (`lib/homunculus-dir.js` `resolveHomunculusDir`). The one Python subprocess this plugin runs sees the same directory through the `CLV2_HOMUNCULUS_DIR` environment variable instead (`lib/project.js` `buildPythonEnv`), so the two never disagree about where it is.

```
<homunculus>/
├── projects.json                           # ECC's own project registry; cleanupProjects edits it
├── instincts/                              # the shared global bucket, readable by every project
│   ├── personal/<id>.md                    # written by promoteStep / /promote, or /instinct import --scope global
│   ├── inherited/<id>.md
│   └── archive/<id>.md
├── board-pointer-<sha256(project directory)[0:12]>.json   # plugin addition: points at a project's board-state.json
├── archive/projects/<project-hash>/        # plugin addition: cleanupProjects archives a stale, zero-instinct project dir here; never deleted
└── projects/<project-hash>/
    ├── observations.jsonl          # tool_start / tool_complete / user_prompt records
    ├── observations.archive/       # rotated out at 10 MB
    ├── observer.log                # plugin addition: one line per observer run
    ├── maintenance.log             # plugin addition: one line per maintenance event
    ├── .observer-state.json        # plugin addition: last run time + line count for the gate
    ├── .activity.json              # plugin addition: last-observed/applied/fired-today/fired-this-week counters
    ├── .settings.json              # plugin addition: persisted observer on/off + muted instinct ids
    ├── fired-misses.log            # plugin addition: near-miss (1-2 shared word) fired-match log, capped at 200 lines
    ├── board-state.json            # plugin addition: the board's three-block summary
    ├── usage.json                  # plugin addition: skill/command/agent usage counts
    ├── evolved/<cluster-id>.md     # plugin addition: candidates proposed/installed/archived by the evolve lifecycle
    └── instincts/
        ├── personal/<id>.md        # written by the observer
        ├── inherited/<id>.md       # written by /instinct import
        ├── pending/<id>.md         # unproven instincts (the 50% rule); never injected
        └── archive/<id>.md         # instincts the maintenance loop decayed below 0.4 confidence, or /instinct wrong archived; never deleted
```

When project resolution fails (python not found on `PATH`, or any other `detect_project()` error), `lib/project.js`'s `globalFallback` sets `project_dir` to the homunculus directory itself, so every file listed under `projects/<project-hash>/` above is instead written directly at the homunculus root; `instincts_personal`/`instincts_inherited` likewise point at the same `instincts/personal`/`instincts/inherited` shown above. In this fallback, the per-project bookkeeping and the shared global bucket end up sharing one directory.
