# How this differs from ECC

This page covers how this plugin's implementation differs from upstream ECC's own `continuous-learning-v2` skill. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

ECC's `continuous-learning-v2` skill is built for Claude Code: a bash hook (`observe.sh`) appends observations on every `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` event, and a separate daemon (`observer-loop.sh`) periodically spawns a real Claude Code sub-agent (with `Read`/`Write` tools) that analyzes observations and writes instinct files itself.

OpenCode has no hook-daemon model and `ctx.generate.text` has no tools, so this plugin:

- Observes through OpenCode's own `tool.hook`/`session.hook("prompt")` instead of a shell script (`lib/observe.js`).
- Injects through `session.hook("context")` instead of editing prompt text, and runs its own maintenance sweep (promote/prune/decay/dedupe/evolve/repair/cleanupProjects) in-process on a timer, instead of relying on someone to run the CLI's equivalent commands by hand (`lib/inject.js`, `lib/maintain.js`).
- Runs the observer in-process, as a single `generate.text` call triggered from inside the plugin (no daemon, no separate process to start or supervise). Since the model has no tools, the plugin itself parses the model's markdown output and writes the instinct files (`lib/observer.js`).
- Installs nothing beyond the plugin itself: no hooks are added to any Claude Code `settings.json`, no scripts are copied anywhere.

`vendor/ecc/instinct-cli.py` (status/import/export/evolve/promote/projects/prune) is used unmodified, so instincts written by this plugin are fully compatible with ECC's own tooling. The vendored CLI's own `evolve --generate` is never run by this plugin: the `/evolve` lifecycle (see [evolve.md](evolve.md)) is a separate, JS-only reimplementation that the CLI's own evolve output was never wired to read.

The instinct model, CLI, and observer prompt are from [affaan-m/ECC](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC), vendored verbatim at commit `ef648e01899ba3e8dc6371642deaaf64b4477775` (MIT License; see `NOTICE`).

# Evolve: from habits to skills

This page covers the candidate lifecycle, the `/evolve` grammar, the TUI picker, install locations and markers, usage tracking, and pruning. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

Nothing this plugin learns ever becomes a real skill, command, agent, or AGENTS.md rule by itself. The weekly `evolve` maintenance step only ever *proposes* a candidate (`lib/maintain.js` `evolveStep`); everything past that point is a command you type.

## Lifecycle

A candidate moves through exactly three statuses, stored on the candidate file itself (`<project data dir>/evolved/<cluster-id>.md`, frontmatter `status:`; `lib/candidates.js` `CANDIDATE_STATUSES`):

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| proposed | The weekly evolve step wrote (or updated) it. Nothing outside `evolved/` exists yet. |
| installed | `/evolve <n\|id> install` copied its drafted artefact to a real location; `installed_at` is stamped. |
| archived | Either rejected before ever being installed (`/evolve <n\|id> reject`, with an optional reason) or removed after being installed (`/evolve <n\|id> archive`). An archived candidate blocks its own cluster from ever being re-proposed. |

Re-running the weekly evolve step (or `/evolve now`) never duplicates a candidate: if a freshly computed cluster's members overlap an existing candidate's own members by 70% or more (`CANDIDATE_MEMBER_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD`, `lib/maintain.js`), that candidate's `members` list is refreshed in place instead of a second candidate being written for the same cluster.

## Kinds

Each cluster of 3+ related instincts (`EVOLVE_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE`, `lib/maintain.js`) sharing significant trigger/summary words (`EVOLVE_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD = 0.3`, `lib/maintain.js`) is proposed as one of four kinds, chosen from the cluster's own size and content, with no model call (`lib/candidates.js` `selectCandidateKind`):

| Cluster | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| 3 members | **rule**: a 1-3 line AGENTS.md snippet, one bullet per member. |
| 4-5 members, summaries read as run/check/verify/test/lint/build/scan steps | **command**: a `commands/<name>.md` draft (`description:` frontmatter, then the steps). |
| 4-5 members, otherwise | **skill**: a full `SKILL.md` draft (`name:`/`description:` frontmatter, member summaries as `## Rules`). |
| 6+ members | **skill**. |
| any size, if a member mentions delegation or a specialist role | **agent**: an agent markdown draft (`description:`/`mode: subagent` frontmatter, member summaries as responsibilities). This overrides every size rule above. |

## The `/evolve` grammar

Token order is free (`/evolve install 2` is the same as `/evolve 2 install`); a bare digit is a pick index, a verb word is the verb, and the first remaining token is the pick id (`lib/evolve-command.js` `EVOLVE_VERBS`/`USAGE`, `lib/evolve-command.js` `parseEvolveArgs`).

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/evolve` | Dashboard: every candidate (proposed/installed/archived), with status, kind, member count, usage, and age; falls back to the deterministic cluster preview when nothing is proposed yet. Changes nothing. |
| `/evolve <n\|id>` | Detail of one candidate: kind, target path, members, full drafted body, plus a next-step hint line. `n` is the number shown by the dashboard (or the board's own numbered hints); `id` works too and never goes stale. Changes nothing. |
| `/evolve <n\|id> install` | Look-before-leap install (see below). |
| `/evolve <n\|id> reject [why]` | Archive a `proposed` candidate without installing it, with an optional reason; every token after `reject` is taken verbatim as the reason, however it looks. |
| `/evolve <n\|id> archive` | Archive any non-archived candidate; for an installed one, also removes the file it installed, but only when ownership and content still match exactly what was installed. |
| `/evolve now` | Run the weekly `evolve` (propose/refresh candidates from today's clusters) and `pruneCandidates` maintenance steps immediately. |
| `/evolve clusters [N]` | The deterministic preview (no model call, no `instinct-cli.py`) of today's top instinct clusters: member ids, average confidence, a "why" naming the words they share, and a suggested form sized by cluster. `--limit N` is also accepted. |
| `/evolve purge` | Move the draft files `/evolve` never lists into `evolved/.purged-<time>/`, each keeping its relative path (undo: move them back): the vendored CLI's `evolve --generate` tree under `evolved/skills/`, `evolved/commands/` and `evolved/agents/`, any other subfolder of `evolved/`, and top-level `.md` files that are not candidates (`lib/candidates.js` `listStrayDrafts`, `moveStrayDrafts`). The first call lists them and moves nothing; the same command again moves them only within 2 minutes (`PURGE_CONFIRM_TTL_MS`) and only when every listed file still has the path, size and modification time it was shown with, and shows the listing again otherwise. A file that cannot move is named in the reply (`failed N: <path> (<code>)`) while the rest move. Candidate files of every status are kept: an archived one is what stops the weekly step proposing its cluster again, and a proposed one has `reject`. |

### Look-before-leap install

`install` is deliberately look-before-leap (`lib/evolve-command.js` `runInstall`): the first call against a candidate (or any call after its body changed since) only re-renders that same detail and asks for the command again ("Run `/evolve <ref> install` again to install."); a repeat against that exact, unchanged candidate is what actually writes it, as a real skill, command, agent, or AGENTS.md rule. This guarantees there is always a preview (what it is, where it would go, every member instinct behind it, and its full body) immediately before the write, within the same running process. Refuses outright if the target is a symlink, or already exists and was not written by this plugin for this exact candidate (see "Install locations and markers" below).

The five commands `/evolve-list [id]`, `/evolve-show <id>`, `/evolve-install <id> [--yes]`, `/evolve-reject <id> [reason]`, and `/evolve-archive <id>`, from v0.10.0 and earlier, remain registered for one release as deprecated aliases that forward their old argv shape straight into the grammar above, each prefixing its reply with a one-line deprecation notice (`lib/commands.js`).

## The TUI picker

On the OpenCode 2 TUI, typing `/evolve` with no arguments opens a pick-a-candidate / pick-an-action / confirm flow instead of the server's text dashboard, so a human never types an id or a 1-based index by hand (`tui.js` `mountEvolvePicker`/`runEvolvePicker`, `lib/evolve-picker.js`). Every write still happens through the server's own `/evolve` command with its own gates; the picker only ever assembles the exact `/evolve ...` text that command already accepts (`lib/evolve-picker.js` `commandTextFor`) and dispatches it through `ctx.client.session.command()`, the same call a typed slash command resolves to. Feature-detected on `ctx.keymap.layer`, `ctx.ui.dialog.select`, and `ctx.ui.slot`; any one missing and nothing here mounts, leaving the server's own dashboard untouched.

Flow: pick a candidate (or "propose from clusters" / "show clusters" / "open the text dashboard"), then pick an action (show / install / reject / archive, filtered by the candidate's own status the same way the server would refuse them), confirm when the action needs one, then dispatch. Install's confirm message never promises a write on that exact confirm ("Shows the detail first; pick Install again to write it."), since the picker cannot tell from its own side whether a given dispatch landed on the arming half or the writing half of the server's look-before-leap gate.

### Open question: slash-name precedence

No documented rule covers what happens when a server-registered command (`lib/commands.js`) and a TUI keymap layer's `slash: { name: "evolve" }` (`tui.js`) share the exact same name. Two outcomes are possible: either the TUI layer wins the name, in which case any non-empty typed input is forwarded unchanged to the server command, so `/evolve 2 install` typed by hand behaves identically to before; or the server command wins outright, in which case the picker never activates and typing `/evolve` falls back to the pre-existing text dashboard. `tui.js` is written so either outcome is safe, but which one actually happens could not be confirmed without a live TUI host.

## Install locations and markers

| Kind | Default location | Override |
| --- | --- | --- |
| skill | `~/.config/opencode/skills/<suggested_name>/SKILL.md` | `evolve.targets.skill` (an absolute directory) |
| command | `~/.config/opencode/commands/<suggested_name>.md` | `evolve.targets.command` |
| agent | `~/.config/opencode/agents/<suggested_name>.md` | `evolve.targets.agent` |
| rule | `<project root>/AGENTS.md`, appended under `## Learned rules (mighty-instincts)` | `evolve.targets.rule` (an absolute file) |

(`lib/candidates.js` `resolveEvolveTargets`/`installPathFor`/`resolveRuleFile`.) Every `evolve.targets.*` override must be absolute once `~` is expanded; a relative value is rejected (with a one-time warning naming which target) and the real default location is used instead.

Every file `install` writes carries three identifying fields in its own frontmatter (`lib/candidates.js` `GENERATED_BY_MARKER`/`injectGeneratedMarkers`): `generated_by: mighty-instincts`, `candidate_id: <this candidate's id>`, and `project_id: <the project that installed it>`, plus `members: [<member instinct ids>]`. A rule's AGENTS.md snippet carries the same `candidate_id`/`project_id` pair instead, on a bracketing pair of HTML comments (`lib/candidates.js`), so removing one candidate's rule can never eat into a neighbouring one's, or into text typed by hand under that heading. `install` also records a sha256 `installed_hash` of exactly what it wrote.

Before touching anything, `install` and `archive` both check: the target is not a symlink; its frontmatter (or, for a rule, its start marker) carries this exact `candidate_id` and `project_id`; and, for `archive` only, that the file's content still hashes to its own recorded `installed_hash` (otherwise a human has edited it since, and it is left alone) (`lib/candidates.js`). Any mismatch refuses the write (install) or leaves the file in place with a note (archive); the file is never silently clobbered or deleted.

## Usage tracking

`<project data dir>/usage.json` counts every skill/command/agent actually used, generated by this plugin or not: the `skill` tool's own calls by `input.id` (or `input.name`), slash commands by name whenever a prompt starts with `/`, and subagent spawns (`subagent`/`task` tool) by `input.agent` (or `input.subagent_type`) (`lib/observe.js` `trackToolUsage`/`trackCommandUsage`, `lib/usage.js` `bumpUsage`). This depends on the host naming its tools and input fields one of those ways; a host that names them differently simply never registers usage for that kind, which is why pruning below treats a kind's entirely-empty usage bucket as "the signal looks dead", not as proof every installed candidate of that kind is unused (`lib/usage.js` `isUsageBucketEmpty`). `/evolve`'s dashboard and the board both read an installed candidate's own usage back by its `suggested_name`.

Command-usage counting runs inside the same `observePrompts` gate as prompt observation (`lib/observe.js` `trackCommandUsage` is only ever called from the `observePrompts` branch of `registerObserve`): setting `observePrompts: false` also turns off command-usage counting, so every installed command candidate's usage bucket looks entirely empty, which is exactly the "signal looks dead" case pruning above refuses to act on.

### Feedback

Whenever an installed candidate's `suggested_name` is actually used, every one of its member instincts gets its `fired` count bumped, wherever that member lives (project personal, inherited, or the shared global bucket) (`lib/observe.js` `applyCandidateFeedback`). A member that has fired at least once is exempt from the maintenance loop's `decay` step, so the habits behind a useful artefact never decay just because people now reach for the artefact instead of the injected instinct directly.

## Pruning (report-only by default)

The weekly evolve step also runs `pruneCandidates` (`lib/maintain.js` `pruneCandidatesStep`): any *installed* candidate with zero uses in `prune.unusedDays` days (default 30, and only once it has been installed at least that long) is flagged, never touched, unless `prune.auto` is explicitly turned on, in which case it is archived and its installed file removed (the same ownership- and hash-gated removal `archive` does). Even in auto mode, a kind whose usage bucket is entirely empty is never auto-archived, and every candidate is handled in its own try/catch, so one failure is logged and skipped rather than aborting the rest of the sweep. Rule candidates are never flagged this way: an AGENTS.md line has no runtime "it was used" signal to measure. `/evolve`'s dashboard separately reports hand-written assets (skills/commands/agents that never carried the `generated_by` marker in the first place) with zero uses in the same window, under "unused (not generated)" (`lib/evolve-command.js`); these are never archived or removed, automatically or otherwise, since this plugin did not write them.

# Instinct

This page covers the `/instinct <verb>` command family, `.settings.json`, why/keep/wrong semantics, muting, doctor, and injection's rules and fired heuristic. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

## Verbs

One command, `/instinct <verb> [args]` (`lib/commands-instinct.js` the `VERBS` table, also the dispatch table), run with no arguments (or `help`) for the full list:

| Verb | Usage | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| status | `status` | Show ECC instinct status (project-scoped + global). |
| projects | `projects` | List known projects and their instinct counts. |
| export | `export [...]` | Export instincts to stdout or a file. |
| import | `import <file\|url> [...]` | Import instincts from a local file or an https URL. |
| observe | `observe` | Run the instinct observer now, ignoring the configured thresholds. |
| why | `why` | Show the ids, confidence and source of the latest injected block for this session, and which ids fired on the last prompt. |
| keep | `keep <id>` | Confirm an instinct was useful: bumps its fired count and raises its confidence by 0.05 (capped at 0.95). |
| wrong | `wrong <id>` | Archive an instinct and mute it so no copy of it is injected again (undo: `/instinct unmute <id>`). |
| mute | `mute <id>` | Skip an id for injection, without archiving its file. |
| unmute | `unmute <id>` | Un-skip a muted id, restoring it from the archive if `wrong` put it there. |
| observer | `observer on\|off` | Turn the background observer on or off; persisted across restarts and applied immediately. |
| doctor | `doctor` | Run the board's own health checks, plus the observer gate's current verdict. |
| help | `help` | List every registered command and `/instinct` verb (also runs for the bare `/instinct`). |

The five commands `/instinct-status`, `/instinct-import`, `/instinct-export`, `/instinct-projects`, and `/instinct-observe`, from v0.10.0 and earlier, remain registered for one release as deprecated aliases that forward their argv text onto the matching verb through the same dispatcher (`lib/commands.js` `INSTINCT_ALIASES`). `/instinct-prune` is not part of this family; it forwards into `/maintain prune` instead (see [maintenance.md](maintenance.md)).

## `.settings.json`

Lives at `<project.project_dir>/.settings.json`, written atomically (`lib/settings.js`):

```json
{
  "observer": { "enabled": true },
  "muted": ["some-instinct-id"]
}
```

`observer.enabled`, when present, overrides `opencode.json`'s own `observer.enabled` for this project, applied to the live `options` object immediately with no restart needed (`lib/settings.js` `applyRuntimeSettings`). `muted` is the list `/instinct mute`/`wrong`/`unmute` maintain; it is merged into `inject.exclude` for injection purposes (`lib/inject.js` `mergeExclude`). A missing or corrupt file reads back as empty defaults rather than throwing.

## `why`, `keep`, `wrong` semantics

| Verb | Does |
| --- | --- |
| why | Reports the most recent injected block for this session (from `lib/inject.js`'s in-memory `lastInjected`), listing each injected id with its confidence percentage and source (`personal`/`inherited`/`global`), then which of them actually fired on the last prompt (`lib/commands-instinct.js` `formatWhy`). |
| keep | Bumps the instinct's `fired` count, then raises its confidence by 0.05 (capped at 0.95), and invalidates the injection pool cache so the change is reflected on the very next request. Works on an instinct in this project's personal/inherited store or the shared global store; refuses (with a pointer to edit by hand) when the id lives inside a multi-block file (an ECC import/export batch) (`lib/commands-instinct.js` `verbKeep`). |
| wrong | Moves the instinct's file to the sibling `archive/` directory (never deletes it) and adds the id to `.settings.json`'s `muted` list, so no copy of it (personal, inherited, or global) is injected again. `/instinct unmute <id>` reverses both halves: it removes the id from `muted` and, if `wrong` archived a copy, restores it from whichever archive (project or global) actually holds it (`lib/commands-instinct.js` `verbWrong`). |

## Muting

`mute`/`unmute` only touch `.settings.json`'s `muted` list; they never move or archive a file (`lib/commands-instinct.js`). A muted id is excluded from injection exactly like one listed in `inject.exclude`, whether it lives in this project's own store or the shared global one.

## `doctor`

Runs the board's own health checks (`lib/health.js`'s `collectHealth`, see [board.md](board.md)'s Health block) plus the observer gate's current verdict (ready, or blocked with a reason) (`lib/commands-instinct.js` `verbDoctor`). When the gate reads `disabled`, it also names whether `.settings.json` is the thing overriding `opencode.json`'s own `observer.enabled`, so the two possible causes of "disabled" are never ambiguous.

## Injection rules

When `inject.enabled` is `true` (the default), every outgoing model request is checked against this project's instincts plus the shared global bucket (`lib/inject.js` `registerInject`/`handleContext`). Up to `inject.max` instincts (default 5) meeting `inject.minConfidence` (default 0.8), excluding any id listed in `inject.exclude` or muted, are added as one more system-context entry:

```
<instincts> learned habits for this project
- <one-line summary of what to do>
...
</instincts>
```

This runs on `ctx.session.hook("context", ...)`, not `"prompt"`: it only ever appends to the request's own `system` array, right before the model sees it, and never edits the user's prompt text or message history (`lib/inject.js`). Because of that there is no cadence to configure and nothing to track between requests; every request gets a block built fresh from whatever instinct files exist right now. The whole block is kept under 1200 characters (`BLOCK_CHAR_BUDGET`, `lib/inject.js` `formatInjectionBlock`), dropping the lowest-confidence entries first if it would not otherwise fit. No model call is involved: this only reads instinct files already on disk. Injection is skipped when the latest user message in the request carries `opencode_loop_v2` or `ulw` metadata (a loop/ultrawork re-prompt, not a fresh request), or when the project has no instincts at all. A trigger that still contains a stray `confidence:`/`domain:`/`scope:`/`source:` is treated as malformed and skipped, with a one-time warning logged.

Each line's summary is the instinct's own `summary:` frontmatter field (one imperative sentence, at most 120 characters); for an instinct written before 0.7.0 with no `summary:` of its own, it falls back to the first sentence of the `## Action` section, clipped to 120 characters (`lib/store.js` `firstActionSentence`).

## The fired heuristic

When an included instinct's `trigger` shares at least 3 significant words (5+ letters, case-insensitive, common filler words removed; `MIN_WORD_LEN`/`MIN_SHARED_WORDS`, `lib/inject.js`) with the latest user message, that instinct's `fired` count is incremented, and the day's total plus a rolling 7-day total are both kept in `.activity.json` (`lib/inject.js` `bumpFiredForMatches`, `lib/activity.js` `recordFired`), shown on the board as "used today / this week". A pending instinct (the 50% rule) is checked for firing exactly the same way, but is never included in the injected block itself; once it fires, the maintenance loop promotes it to a real instinct (`lib/maintain.js` `graduatePendingStep`). This is counted once per human prompt in a top-level session, never per tool-call step within that same turn, and never for a subagent or other child session (one with a parentID, `lib/inject.js` `isChildSession`). A headless top-level session, one with no parentID at all, has no human typing into it either, but is still counted the same as any other top-level session: `isChildSession` only ever checks for a parentID, so this plugin's own `/skill-review` session (spawned with no parent) counts too.

A candidate that shares 1 or 2 significant words (just under the 3-word threshold) is logged instead to `fired-misses.log` (id, shared-word count, the words themselves; capped at 200 lines), for tuning that threshold later; nothing in this plugin ever reads that log back (`lib/inject.js`).

# Maintenance

This page covers the background sweep's steps and numbers, the `/maintain` and `/promote` commands, and dry-run. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

A background sweep keeps the instinct stores tidy without anyone ever running a command. It runs right after every observer run, and otherwise at least every `maintenance.intervalHours` (default 24), guarded against overlapping with itself (`lib/maintain.js` `createMaintenanceController`). Every step below is on by default (`MAINTENANCE_DEFAULTS`, `lib/maintain.js`) and logs what it did to `maintenance.log`; any one can be turned off independently (`maintenance.promote: false`, etc.).

```json
{
  "intervalHours": 24,
  "dryRun": false,
  "promote": true,
  "prune": true,
  "decay": true,
  "dedupe": true,
  "evolve": true,
  "repair": true,
  "cleanupProjects": true
}
```

## Steps, in run order

Run order follows `runMaintenance` (`lib/maintain.js`): repair, prune, decay, promote, graduate-pending, then evolve and cleanupProjects (both gated on their own cadence).

### promote (`lib/maintain.js` `promoteStep`)

Either of two independent qualification paths copies an instinct to the shared global bucket, whichever one it clears first:

| Path | Qualifies when |
| --- | --- |
| Cross-project corroboration (ECC's own rule) | Confident enough (`>= 0.8`, `PROMOTE_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`) and whose id (or a trigger with 70%+ word overlap, `PROMOTE_TRIGGER_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD`) appears in 2+ distinct project stores (`PROMOTE_MIN_PROJECTS`). |
| Proven on its own, no corroboration needed | Confidence `>= 0.9` (`PROMOTE_FIRED_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`) and fired `>= 3` times (`PROMOTE_FIRED_THRESHOLD`), in a single project. |

Neither path promotes an instinct whose trigger names a repository (any project name in `projects.json`, or the instinct's own `project_name`, as a whole word; `lib/maintain.js` `namesRepository`), since a global copy is injected into every project, nor an id found in an `instincts/archive/` folder (the global one or any project's), so a retired copy is never brought back. Reimplemented directly over `projects/*/instincts/personal/*.md`; never shells out to Python for this.

### prune (`lib/maintain.js` `pruneStep`)

Deletes files in `instincts/pending/` older than 30 days (`PENDING_TTL_DAYS`, ECC's own default pending TTL); logs a warning for ones within 7 days of expiring (`PENDING_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS`).

### decay (`lib/maintain.js` `decayStep`)

A personal instinct that has never fired, past 30 days old (`DECAY_GRACE_DAYS`), loses 0.05 confidence (`DECAY_STEP`) per full week since its last decay; once that drops it below 0.4 (`DECAY_ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD`) it is moved (never deleted) to `instincts/archive/`.

### dedupe (`lib/maintain.js` `dedupeOrMerge`)

Before the observer writes a new instinct, it is compared against every existing personal instinct on trigger-vs-trigger OR summary-vs-summary word overlap: a close match (`>= 60%` on either field, `DEDUPE_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD`, or `>= 45%` on either field when both also share the same domain, `DEDUPE_SAME_DOMAIN_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD`, and `>= 35%` overlap between the two `## Action` sections, `DEDUPE_ACTION_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD`) gets its confidence raised and the new evidence appended, keeping its own summary, instead of creating a near-duplicate file. The Action check keeps two instincts that only share the project's own words apart; an instinct with no Action is never merged.

### evolve (`lib/maintain.js` `evolveStep`)

Groups personal instincts by domain and by word overlap into clusters of 3+ (`EVOLVE_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE`, `EVOLVE_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD = 0.3`), and proposes (or updates) one candidate per cluster under `evolved/<cluster-id>.md` (no model call). Runs at most once a week (`EVOLVE_INTERVAL_MS`), regardless of how often the sweep itself runs. See [evolve.md](evolve.md) for the full lifecycle.

### repair (`lib/maintain.js` `repairStep`)

A one-off, idempotent cleanup pass over the personal store: cleans a trigger carrying a leaked trailing frontmatter fragment (e.g. `..., confidence: 0.8`), the shape a parser bug before 0.7.0 (or a hand-edited file) could leave behind; and moves a personal instinct with confidence `<= 0.5` that has never fired into `instincts/pending/`, the 50% rule applied retroactively to anything that landed in personal before that rule covered it.

### cleanupProjects (`lib/maintain.js` `cleanupProjectsStep`)

Runs at most once a day (`CLEANUP_PROJECTS_INTERVAL_MS`). For every entry in ECC's own projects registry (`projects.json`) whose root no longer exists, or lives under the OS temp directory, and which has 0 instincts of its own, the registry entry is removed and its project directory is archived (never deleted outright) to `archive/projects/<id>/`.

## `/maintain` and `/promote`

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/maintain [--dry-run]` | Run the full sweep now: promote/prune/decay/evolve/repair/cleanup. `--dry-run` previews every step, including evolve/cleanup regardless of today's weekly/daily gate, without changing anything (`lib/commands-maintain.js` `buildMaintainCommand`/`runFullSweep`). |
| `/maintain prune [--dry-run]` | Runs only the pending-instinct prune (`lib/commands-maintain.js` `runPruneOnly`). `/instinct-prune` forwards here for one release. |
| `/promote [--yes]` | Preview (default) or run (`--yes`) promoting project-scoped instincts that qualify to global scope, using the same `promoteStep` rule as the sweep (`lib/commands-maintain.js` `buildPromoteCommand`). |

## Trying it safely (dry-run)

Set `"maintenance": { "dryRun": true }` to see exactly what the next sweep would do without changing anything: every line it would otherwise log to `maintenance.log` is prefixed `would` instead (`would promote: ...`, `would archive: ...`, `would merge ... into ...`, and so on), with no file written, moved, or deleted. Turn it back to `false` (the default) once satisfied with what it shows. `/maintain --dry-run` gets the same preview on demand, forcing the weekly/daily gated steps (evolve, cleanupProjects) open for that one preview regardless of today's actual cadence (`lib/maintain.js` the `force`/`dryRun` overrides).

# Observer

This page covers the background instinct-distillation run: events, thresholds, defaults, the model requirement, the backoff table, the zero-write damper, the notify rule, and what gets written where. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the rest of the plugin.

## Defaults

`OBSERVER_DEFAULTS` (`lib/observer.js`):

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "runIntervalMinutes": 15,
  "minObservations": 40,
  "maxAnalysisLines": 300,
  "maxAnalysisBytes": 32768,
  "notify": true
}
```

`model` is omitted above: its real default is unset (`undefined`, not `null`), since JSON cannot carry `undefined`. See "The model requirement" below.

The observer is off by default. It is one of two background steps that actually call a model (the other is the headless session `/skill-review` spawns, see [skill-review.md](skill-review.md)); the observer specifically is also the one that writes new instincts, so it stays opt-in even though the maintenance sweep (see [maintenance.md](maintenance.md)) and prompt injection are both on by default.

## The model requirement

`observer.model` must be a `"provider/model"` string (`lib/observer.js` `parseModelRef`). Left unset, a run attempt stops before calling the model, logs and posts a one-time notice, and every later attempt is skipped at the gate until the option is set and the plugin restarted (`lib/observer.js` `handleModelUnset`). The exact notice text (`lib/observer.js` `MODEL_UNSET_MESSAGE`):

> mighty-instincts: learning runs are paused because observer.model is not set. Add "observer": { "model": "<provider>/<model>" } to the plugin options in opencode.json (a cheap model is enough) and restart.

`/instinct observer on` shows the same sentence when enabling finds no model configured (`lib/commands-instinct.js` `verbObserver`). `lib/health.js`'s doctor check flags `observer.enabled: true` with no model the same way (see [board.md](board.md)'s Health block).

## What runs, in order (`lib/observer.js` `runOnceInner`)

Every observed tool call or prompt checks, cheapest first, against `.observer-state.json` (`lib/observer.js` `evaluateObserverGate`):

1. A consecutive-failure backoff (below) has not yet expired.
2. Enough time has passed since the last run (`runIntervalMinutes`, default 15).
3. Enough new observations have piled up since then (`minObservations`, default 40, doubled to 80 once two runs in a row have each written 0 new instincts, until a run writes something again: the "zero-write damper").
4. Once a previous attempt has already discovered `observer.model` is unset, that hold lifts as soon as `observer.model` parses as a valid `provider/model` string again; it does not wait for a run to actually succeed first (in practice this still needs a restart, since nothing in this plugin ever sets `observer.model` itself while running, see "The model requirement" below).

Once every gate passes, the plugin first gives any personal instinct with no `summary:` field (written before 0.7.0, imported, or hand-written) the first sentence of its own `## Action`, without a model call and without touching its body (`lib/observer.js` `backfillMissingSummaries`). Then:

1. Reads the most recent observation lines, capped at `maxAnalysisLines` (default 300) and `maxAnalysisBytes` (default 32768): the tail is read newest-first until that byte budget is spent, then reordered oldest-first before the model sees it (`lib/observer.js` `buildAnalysisView`), plus the existing instinct list (id, trigger, confidence; never the bodies), so the model updates instincts instead of duplicating them.
2. If `observer.model` is still unset at this point, the run stops here (see "The model requirement" above).
3. Calls `ctx.generate.text({ prompt, model })` once, with no tools available to the model (`lib/observer.js`).
4. Parses `<instinct>...</instinct>` blocks out of the response and validates each one (`lib/observer.js` `parseInstinctBlock`): id (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$`), trigger (rejected outright if it carries a leaked `confidence:`/`domain:`/`scope:`/`source:` fragment), confidence (0 to 1), domain, `summary` (one imperative sentence, required, rejected over 160 characters, trimmed to 120), and no stray `---` in the body.
5. Checks each valid instinct against the existing personal store for a dedupe/merge match (`lib/maintain.js` `dedupeOrMerge`; see "Dedupe thresholds" below).
6. Writes anything left to `instincts/personal/`, except an instinct with confidence `<= 0.5`, which goes to `instincts/pending/` instead (`lib/observer.js` via `classifyNewInstinct`, `lib/maintain.js`): the "50% rule", unproven until it is actually used once.
7. Logs the result to `observer.log`, runs the maintenance sweep, refreshes the board state, and posts a summary into the session when `observer.notify` is true (see "Notify" below).

## Backoff table

A failure anywhere from the model call through the final state save backs off the next attempt (`lib/observer.js` `BACKOFF_STEPS_MS`, `lib/observer.js` `handleRunFailure`):

| Consecutive failure | Next attempt allowed after |
| --- | --- |
| 1st | 5 minutes |
| 2nd | 15 minutes |
| 3rd and every one after | 60 minutes |

A success resets the streak to 0. The first failure of a streak also posts a one-time notice (background run only; a manual `/instinct-observe` or `/instinct observe` gets the same information back as its own reply either way).

## The zero-write damper

Once two runs in a row have each written 0 new instincts, `minObservations` doubles (default 40 -> 80) until a run writes something again (`lib/observer.js`, tracked as `lastWrittenCounts` in `.observer-state.json`).

## Notify rule

`observer.notify` posts a synthetic summary message into the triggering session after a background run. For the background run specifically (not a manual `/instinct-observe`), this is skipped when the run wrote 0 new instincts (`lib/observer.js` `shouldNotify = wantsNotify(...) && (notify === true || written > 0)`); a consecutive-failure notice still posts regardless, once, on the first failure of a streak. A manual trigger (`notify: true`) always gets its reply.

## What is written where

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `observer.log` | One line per run: `<iso> run: <N> written, <N> rejected, model <provider/model>`, with ` ids: <id>,<id>,...` and ` rejected: <reason>; ...` suffixes when applicable (`lib/observer.js`). |
| `.observer-state.json` | Last run time, last line count, consecutive failure count, next allowed attempt, the model-unset block flag, and the last two runs' written counts (`lib/observer-state.js`). |
| `instincts/personal/<id>.md` | A newly written, confident-enough instinct. |
| `instincts/pending/<id>.md` | A newly written instinct with confidence `<= 0.5` (the 50% rule). |

See [data-layout.md](data-layout.md) for the full on-disk layout.

## Cost

This is at most one `generate.text` call per interval, on whatever model is set in `observer.model`. `/instinct observe` (and the deprecated `/instinct-observe` alias) run the same logic on demand, bypassing the interval/count/backoff gates (it still needs `observer.model` set, and still stops with the same notice if it is not).

# Observer Agent

A background agent that analyzes observations from Claude Code sessions to detect patterns and create instincts.

## When to Run

- After enough observations accumulate (configurable, default 20)
- On a scheduled interval (configurable, default 5 minutes)
- When triggered on demand via SIGUSR1 to the observer process

## Input

Reads observations from the **project-scoped** observations file:
- Project: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/projects/<project-hash>/observations.jsonl`
- Global fallback: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/observations.jsonl`

```jsonl
{"timestamp":"2025-01-22T10:30:00Z","event":"tool_start","session":"abc123","tool":"Edit","input":"...","project_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","project_name":"my-react-app"}
{"timestamp":"2025-01-22T10:30:01Z","event":"tool_complete","session":"abc123","tool":"Edit","output":"...","project_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","project_name":"my-react-app"}
{"timestamp":"2025-01-22T10:30:05Z","event":"tool_start","session":"abc123","tool":"Bash","input":"npm test","project_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","project_name":"my-react-app"}
{"timestamp":"2025-01-22T10:30:10Z","event":"tool_complete","session":"abc123","tool":"Bash","output":"All tests pass","project_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","project_name":"my-react-app"}
```

## Pattern Detection

Look for these patterns in observations:

### 1. User Corrections
When a user's follow-up message corrects Claude's previous action:
- "No, use X instead of Y"
- "Actually, I meant..."
- Immediate undo/redo patterns

→ Create instinct: "When doing X, prefer Y"

### 2. Error Resolutions
When an error is followed by a fix:
- Tool output contains error
- Next few tool calls fix it
- Same error type resolved similarly multiple times

→ Create instinct: "When encountering error X, try Y"

### 3. Repeated Workflows
When the same sequence of tools is used multiple times:
- Same tool sequence with similar inputs
- File patterns that change together
- Time-clustered operations

→ Create workflow instinct: "When doing X, follow steps Y, Z, W"

### 4. Tool Preferences
When certain tools are consistently preferred:
- Always uses Grep before Edit
- Prefers Read over Bash cat
- Uses specific Bash commands for certain tasks

→ Create instinct: "When needing X, use tool Y"

## Output

Creates/updates instincts in the **project-scoped** instincts directory:
- Project: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/projects/<project-hash>/instincts/personal/`
- Global: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ecc-homunculus/instincts/personal/` (for universal patterns)

## Scope Decision Guide

When creating instincts, determine scope based on these heuristics:

> **Scope Decision Guide** – See the canonical table under the "Scope Decision Guide" heading in `skills/continuous-learning-v2/SKILL.md`.

**When in doubt, default to `scope: project`** — it's safer to be project-specific and promote later than to contaminate the global space.

## Confidence Calculation

Initial confidence based on observation frequency:
- 1-2 observations: 0.3 (tentative)
- 3-5 observations: 0.5 (moderate)
- 6-10 observations: 0.7 (strong)
- 11+ observations: 0.85 (very strong)

Confidence adjusts over time:
- +0.05 for each confirming observation
- -0.1 for each contradicting observation
- -0.02 per week without observation (decay)

## Instinct Promotion (Project → Global)

An instinct should be promoted from project-scoped to global when:
1. The **same pattern** (by id or similar trigger) exists in **2+ different projects**
2. Average confidence across instances is **>= 0.8**
3. The domain is in the global-friendly list (security, general-best-practices, workflow)

Promotion is handled by the `instinct-cli.py promote` command or the `/evolve` analysis.

## Important Guidelines

1. **Be Conservative**: Only create instincts for clear patterns (3+ observations)
2. **Be Specific**: Narrow triggers are better than broad ones
3. **Track Evidence**: Always include what observations led to the instinct
4. **Respect Privacy**: Never include actual code snippets, only patterns
5. **Merge Similar**: If a new instinct is similar to existing, update rather than duplicate
6. **Default to Project Scope**: Unless the pattern is clearly universal, make it project-scoped
7. **Include Project Context**: Always set `project_id` and `project_name` for project-scoped instincts
